facts.raw_span: stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
metastases of the liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, involving nasolabial folds
Erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Creatine kinase: 1088 U/L
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody: negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers
Grade 4/5 strength on resisted abduction of shoulders bilaterally
Limited flexion of both hips

concepts.why: The patient presents with skin symptoms, including photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption, diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, and erythema and edema of upper eyelids, which are consistent with dermatomyositis, along with elevated creatine kinase levels and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers.

The patient has a history of stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma with metastases, and the development of dermatomyositis-like symptoms may be related to the underlying cancer, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.
The patient has elevated creatine kinase levels, antinuclear antibody positivity, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are consistent with an autoimmune myopathy.
The patient presents with muscle weakness, elevated creatine kinase levels, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are consistent with polymyositis.
The patient has antinuclear antibody positivity and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are consistent with lupus myositis.

The patient has a history of stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma with metastases, and the development of systemic symptoms may be related to the underlying cancer, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.

rationales.F01: The presence of stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma suggests a paraneoplastic syndrome, which is more commonly associated with dermatomyositis.
rationales.F02: The presence of metastases in multiple organs suggests a paraneoplastic syndrome, which is more commonly associated with dermatomyositis.
rationales.F06: The elevated creatine kinase level is a strong indicator of muscle damage, which is consistent with dermatomyositis and polymyositis.
rationales.F07: The presence of antinuclear antibodies with a speckled pattern is more commonly associated with lupus myositis, but can also be seen in dermatomyositis.
rationales.F08: The absence of Jo-1 antibodies makes polymyositis less likely, but does not rule it out entirely.
rationales.F10: The muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers is consistent with dermatomyositis and polymyositis.
